history.summary: Efficiently sized 1,216sqft 4BR in Choa Chu Kang (D23) at just $1.26M and $1,036 PSF (below the $1,062 median), with a strong 6.37%/yr resale CAGR over 138 transactions and 220m to Keat Hong LRT. The highest arena Elo in the batch (2037) — a low-quantum, high-liquidity family unit.
history.rating_rationale: This is a rare cheap-and-genuine 4BR: $1.26M absolute is far below the band-ceiling so the upgrader buyer pool is very deep, PSF 1036 is at/under the 1062 median, and 6.37%/yr over 138 txns is reliable. 220m to Keat Hong LRT (links to NSL at Choa Chu Kang) is convenient. Built 2000 (99LH, ~73yr remaining) is the main caveat — lease decay matters over a long hold — but the value, liquidity and demonstrated appreciation are clearly positive. Top arena performer (Elo 2037, 379-39-0) corroborates.

history.summary: Palm Gardens 3BR, 1,206 sqft at $1,288,000 ($1,068 psf) — a Keppel Land 694-unit 99LH (lease from 1996, 70 yrs left) in deep Choa Chu Kang, 220m to Keat Hong LRT. The algo's 801/1000 and its -16.2% 'age-adjusted district discount' do not survive verification: against the project's OWN URA prints the ask is at market, not below it. Last 12 months, 11 same-size (1,150-1,300 sqft) resales printed a median of $1,280,000 / $1,062 psf — this ask is +0.6% above that, and above the median of every floor band except 16-20. The discount is to the DISTRICT, and it is structural and not closing: Palm Gardens' 3BR band went $1,045 psf (2023) -> $1,060 (2024) -> $1,056 (2025) -> $1,062 (2026), i.e. ~+0.5%/yr, while D23's same-size 99LH resale stock went $1,110 -> $1,126 -> $1,182 -> $1,172 over the identical window. The project has been flat for three years AND has lagged its own district. Entry is honest and liquidity is genuinely deep, but for a 5-7yr resale-profit mandate there is no edge here at $1.288M — it is OCR beta with a 1996 lease clock, bought at full price against ~10-16 near-identical 1,206 sqft 3BRs listed in the same project right now.
history.rating_rationale: VERIFY-FIRST APPLIED, DISCOUNT DID NOT SURVIVE. The MMR 801 is carried by two components — age_value +12.11 and appreciation +7.1 — and both fail verification. (1) age_value credits a -16.2% premium_vs_age_adjusted_median vs the D23 size band. But psf_premium_vs_ura_median_pct is +1.2% (above the project's own median), and the project's own 138 URA prints confirm it: 38 prints in the 1,150-1,300 sqft band since Feb-24 median $1,280,000 / $1,060 psf; the 11 prints in the last 12 months median $1,280,000 / $1,062 psf; 2026 YTD $1,286,000. The $1,288,000 ask is AT market. The gap to the district is a persistent location/vintage discount (Palm Gardens $1,062 vs D23 same-band 99LH $1,172 = -9.4%), sitting mid-pack against its true CCK peer set (Regent Grove $1,003, Northvale $1,107, Regent Heights $1,132, Parkview $972). It is priced correctly for what it is, not mispriced. (2) The 6.37%/yr ura_5yr_cagr is entirely the 2021-23 post-COVID catch-up ($780 -> $1,045 psf); since 2023 the 3BR band has done ~+0.5%/yr. momentum is already flagged -1.0 (worst reading), and per repo priors trailing CAGR has ~zero forward power anyway. The 6.35%/yr ROI projection should not be relied on — override set to 2.5%/yr (OCR baseline 3.7% less ~1.2pp for the demonstrated 3-year district lag and a 1996 lease clock). At 2.5% the 5yr all-cash outcome is roughly +1.5%/yr capital plus ~2.1% net yield after $39.6k entry costs and exit commission — a poor return on $1.29M of locked capital for a profit-seeking mandate. WHY NOT AVOID: nothing here is broken or overpriced. Entry is honest, liquidity is real (138 URA txns across 694 units, deep buyer_pool, ~18-20 same-band resales a year), Keppel Land build with private lift lobbies and full facilities (bowling alley, tennis) that reviews consistently rate well-maintained, quantum is $500k inside the $1.8M budget, OCR is the favoured forward region, and Choa Chu Kang becomes an NSL x Jurong Region Line interchange in mid-2028 — a dated catalyst inside the hold window, 826m away. WHY NOT BUY: he would be paying full price for three years of zero appreciation in a project that underperforms its own district, competing at exit against a large stack of undifferentiated clones. This only becomes a Buy on a negotiated entry: at ~$1.20-1.22M (a real 5-6% below the project's own 12-month median, achievable given how many sellers are cutting) the margin of safety would carry the lease decay and the thesis flips.
red_flags: NO DISCOUNT vs the project's own comps — ask $1,288,000 is +0.6% above the trailing-12mo median print ($1,280,000, n=11) and +1.2% above the URA project median; the algo's -16.2% 'cheapness' is a district comparison, not unit value

THREE YEARS FLAT — Palm Gardens 3BR band median: $1,260k (2023) / $1,280k (2024) / $1,277.5k (2025) / $1,286k (2026) ≈ +0.5%/yr; the 6.37% headline CAGR is all 2021-23 catch-up and momentum is flagged -1.0

UNDERPERFORMS ITS OWN DISTRICT — D23 same-size 99LH resale psf rose $1,110 -> $1,172 (2023-26, +5.6%) while Palm Gardens rose $1,045 -> $1,062 (+1.6%); the structural discount is widening, not converging

HEAVY SAME-TYPE COMPETITION — ~10-16 near-identical 1,206/1,216 sqft 3BRs listed concurrently in the same 694-unit project (blocks 2A/2B/2C/2D/2E/3 Hong San Walk) asking $1.288M-$1.40M, most with recent price cuts; that is ~8-10 months of inventory against ~18-20 band resales/yr, and it is the same wall he must sell into in 5-7 years
LEASE FROM 1996 — 70 yrs left today, 63-65 at exit; an older clock than most D23 peers, and the decay is very likely part of why the project has stalled while the district moved

FLOOR AND FACING UNKNOWN — floor_level and facing are 0% populated in this DB (known broken enricher) and there is no researched stack profile, so the specific unit cannot be placed; URA floor bands show low floors clearing ~$1,255k vs ~$1,299k high, so if this is a low-floor unit the ask is ~$33k over its own band median

NO REALSMART EVIDENCE — realsmart_cache returned a resolved record for palm-gardens with every field null (realscore, pct_profitable, resale_txns, annual_return_pct); per instructions it was not re-fetched, so there is zero downside/profitability evidence from that source
Modest carry — $3,800/mo rent = 3.54% gross, 2.11% net; does not compensate for flat capital
LRT not MRT at the doorstep (Keat Hong 220m); the MRT/JRL interchange is 826m and Tengah's new-town supply competes directly for the same west-region upgrader
catalysts: Choa Chu Kang becomes an NSL x Jurong Region Line interchange — JRL Stage 1 (CCK-Boon Lay/Tawas) now mid-2028 after a six-month LTA delay; a genuine dated catalyst 826m away, inside a 5-7yr hold
Genuinely deep liquidity — 138 URA transactions, 694 units, ~18-20 same-band resales a year and a deep HDB-upgrader pool in Choa Chu Kang; exit is slow-priced but never stuck

Keppel Land build with private lift lobby to each unit — a real differentiator for a 2000-vintage OCR condo — plus full facilities (pool, tennis, basketball, 2-lane bowling alley) and consistently strong maintenance reviews (9.2/10 on SingaporeExpats)
OCR is the backtested-favoured forward region (+3.7%/yr realized vs RCR +3.1, CCR +1.9)
$1.288M quantum sits ~$500k inside the $1.8M budget, keeping the buyer pool at exit very deep and leaving headroom to negotiate or to fund a better alternative
Tengah new-town build-out and the wider west-region masterplan lift the whole CCK catchment — but as beta, and Tengah is also competing supply

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: $3,800/mo from ura_project_bed (confidence 0.95) = 3.54% gross / 2.11% net. Sits mid-range against EdgeProp's quoted $2.10-$3.90 psf/mo for the project ($3.15 psf here). Credible and not an artifact — no >5.5% yield flag. But this is carry only: the repo's own backtest finds high gross yield predicts LOWER forward price growth (std_β -0.16), and 2.11% net does not compensate for a project appreciating at ~0.5%/yr.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: The 6.37%/yr ura_5yr_cagr (138 txns, data_confidence 1.0) is arithmetically real but structurally misleading — it is the 2021-23 recovery ($780 -> $1,011 -> $1,045 psf) with a three-year plateau bolted on the end. Project 3BR-band medians: 2023 $1,045 psf / $1,260k, 2024 $1,060 / $1,280k, 2025 $1,056 / $1,277.5k, 2026 YTD $1,062 / $1,286k. Over the same window D23's same-size 99LH stock ran $1,110 -> $1,126 -> $1,182 -> $1,172, so the project lagged its district by ~4pp cumulative. momentum is already -1.0. Override to 2.5%/yr on resale-to-resale URA evidence: OCR baseline 3.7% less ~1.2pp for the demonstrated lag and the 1996 lease clock. Do not underwrite this at 6.37%.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No researched profile for Palm Gardens (stack_profile.status = not_researched) and floor_level/facing are 0% populated in this DB, so the unit's stack, floor and outlook are unknown — this is a stated data gap, not an assumption of a good or bad floor. What can be said from URA floor bands (1,150-1,300 sqft, since Feb-24): 01-05 median $1,255k (n=9, $1.100-1.315M), 06-10 $1,260k (n=8), 11-15 $1,280k (n=15), 16-20 $1,299k (n=6). The floor premium is modest (~3.5% low-to-high), so floor uncertainty is less damaging here than usual — but it does mean $1,288,000 is above the median of every band except 16-20. Worth running /research-development before any offer, and worth asking the agent for the exact floor: a 03-floor unit at this ask is straightforwardly overpaying.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: Resale-to-resale URA prints only (data/ura_district_D23.csv, 138 Palm Gardens rows). Project 3BR-band (1,150-1,300 sqft) medians 2023 $1,260k -> 2026 YTD $1,286k = ~+0.7%/yr; D23 same-size 99LH resale $1,110 -> $1,172 psf = ~+1.8%/yr over the same window. Set at 2.5%/yr = OCR regional baseline 3.7% less ~1.2pp for the project's measured 3-year lag vs its district and accelerating decay on a 1996 lease. No portal headline CAGR used.
